log.text: Vale sits with Aethra and the Argive mothers. Their sons died in the attack on Thebes. They ask Athens to recover the remains for burial. Aethra sets their petition and olive branch within reach.

log.speaker: World
log.text: Vale asks Theseus to send a herald with a burial truce. The proposal names the dead, a return road and witnesses from both sides. Theseus agrees to seek those terms.

log.speaker: World
log.text: Theseus reads the herald’s return to Vale. In this new telling, both sides accepted the burial truce. The remains reached Eleusis under witness. The mothers now have their dead; their funeral and care still lie before them.

log.speaker: World
log.text: Aethra tells Vale the funeral’s further loss. Evadne died at Capaneus’s pyre despite Iphis’s plea. He has lost both his children. The surviving children carry ashes and speak of vengeance. Aethra recalls the play’s closing oath: Argos owes Athens aid, while Athena names another war for the children. Iphis comes to sit beside the shrine steps.

log.speaker: World

log.speaker: World
log.text: The keeper names an earlier time, before the deaths of the Theban brothers. In Sophocles’s tale, blind Oedipus reaches this grove with Antigone. The townspeople fear his name. Theseus grants him shelter. Vale listens at the present boundary stone.

log.speaker: World
log.text: Vale sets the water cup and honey beside the grove. The keeper recalls the gentle offering taught to Oedipus, which Ismene made in the earlier tale. Today’s gift rests at the same boundary for the keeper’s rite.

log.speaker: World
log.text: The keeper continues the earlier tale. Creon seized Antigone and Ismene to force their father’s return. Theseus brought them back. Polyneices then sought his father’s blessing for war. Oedipus refused and cursed both sons. Vale hears how care and power crossed these paths.

log.speaker: World
log.text: The keeper finishes the tale. Oedipus entrusted his final place to Theseus alone. His daughters mourned and returned toward Thebes. Theseus kept the place secret and promised them care. Vale hears the public promise while the old resting place keeps its silence.

log.speaker: World
log.text: The keeper opens a separate tale after Heracles’s death, under Demophon, son of Theseus. Iolaus and the children sought shelter here. Eurystheus’s herald claimed them and used force. Demophon upheld the altar’s protection. Vale hears the claim beside the present shrine.

log.speaker: World
log.text: Vale lays the blanket from Piraeus beside the altar. The keeper sets it aside for present-day guests. The old tale continues beside a place made ready for someone who may need it.

log.speaker: World
log.text: In the tale, an oracle demanded a noble maiden’s life. Demophon refused to compel a household. Heracles’s daughter offered herself for her siblings and rejected a lottery. The keeper gives her reasons their full place, then names the life the city’s safety cost. Vale listens.

log.speaker: World
log.text: The keeper tells the next part. The daughter’s sacrifice preceded the battle. Athens won; Iolaus pursued Eurystheus, who was brought back alive. The messenger distinguished what he saw from the story of Iolaus’s renewed youth. Vale hears the cost before the victory.

log.speaker: World
log.text: The keeper sets out the final dispute. Alcmene demands Eurystheus’s death. The city’s rule protects a prisoner taken alive. Eurystheus defends his choices and foretells his grave’s power. Vale may hear the source ending or ask the keeper for a hearing variation.

log.speaker: World
log.text: Vale asks the keeper for a changed ending. In this new telling, Demophon holds Eurystheus for a public hearing under the city’s rule. Alcmene keeps her claim and her anger. The keeper marks the change, while the daughter’s loss remains part of both accounts.

World: Vale sets the water cup and honey beside the grove. The keeper recalls the gentle offering taught to Oedipus, which Ismene made in the earlier tale. Today’s gift rests at the same boundary for the keeper’s rite.

World: The keeper continues the earlier tale. Creon seized Antigone and Ismene to force their father’s return. Theseus brought them back. Polyneices then sought his father’s blessing for war. Oedipus refused and cursed both sons. Vale hears how care and power crossed these paths.

World: The keeper finishes the tale. Oedipus entrusted his final place to Theseus alone. His daughters mourned and returned toward Thebes. Theseus kept the place secret and promised them care. Vale hears the public promise while the old resting place keeps its silence.
World: Vale sets the refuge tablet beside the keeper. Together they record a present custom: hear a stranger’s need, offer rest and seek protection. The old tale gives this promise its weight.

World: The keeper opens a separate tale after Heracles’s death, under Demophon, son of Theseus. Iolaus and the children sought shelter here. Eurystheus’s herald claimed them and used force. Demophon upheld the altar’s protection. Vale hears the claim beside the present shrine.
World: Vale lays the blanket from Piraeus beside the altar. The keeper sets it aside for present-day guests. The old tale continues beside a place made ready for someone who may need it.

World: In the tale, an oracle demanded a noble maiden’s life. Demophon refused to compel a household. Heracles’s daughter offered herself for her siblings and rejected a lottery. The keeper gives her reasons their full place, then names the life the city’s safety cost. Vale listens.

World: The keeper tells the next part. The daughter’s sacrifice preceded the battle. Athens won; Iolaus pursued Eurystheus, who was brought back alive. The messenger distinguished what he saw from the story of Iolaus’s renewed youth. Vale hears the cost before the victory.

World: The keeper sets out the final dispute. Alcmene demands Eurystheus’s death. The city’s rule protects a prisoner taken alive. Eurystheus defends his choices and foretells his grave’s power. Vale may hear the source ending or ask the keeper for a hearing variation.
